summary: The returned string has Theta(log k) digits, giving an output-size lower bound that the accepted direct binary mapping matches.

optimality.argument: The k-th lucky number has m = floor(log2(k + 1)) characters, and returning it requires writing all m characters. The accepted source converts k + 1 to its m + 1 binary digits and maps each of the final m bits once, so it uses O(m) = O(log k) time.

replacement_checks.evidence: Any correct implementation must materialize each of the m characters in the required string, establishing Omega(m) worst-case time.
Binary conversion and the one-pass zero-to-four and one-to-seven mapping each process O(m) digits.
Regression enumerates every lucky string through ten digits independently, checks transitions between output lengths, and verifies the maximum legal k.
